ThingDef.label: vekkra choker
ThingDef.description: A small, deadly mushroom that steadily breathes polluting toxic spores into the air around it. Anything not immune to poison that stands near one long enough chokes; it is the little cousin of the grath elder and it guards nothing but itself.

ThingDef.label: sikkra lure
ThingDef.description: Tiny caps that light up a cold teal in the dark to draw small prey, which lands, sticks to the gills and is slowly digested. Whole swarms of gnats die to a single patch; the light is the trap.

ThingDef.label: pimmik mold
ThingDef.description: The fruiting bodies of a pale mold that carpets the forest floor wherever the mat is warm: a fuzz of tiny pins, each with a bead of a head. It is the most common thing in the biome and the least noticed.

ThingDef.label: nissik gill
ThingDef.description: A near-black cap whose gills glow brightly beneath it, so that it lights the milk it stands in and nothing above. It grows in the shallows or in ground wet enough to pass for them.

ThingDef.label: nissik gill
ThingDef.description: While its cap's exterior is largely dark in color, its underside glows brightly. It grows most often in water or extremely wet environments.

ThingDef.label: rukka cap
ThingDef.description: A damp-ground mushroom with a cap wrinkled like a walnut, glowing a soft lilac from the folds. It is the grazers' staple; anything that eats fungus eats this first.

ThingDef.label: rukka cap
ThingDef.description: A subterranean fungus that grows in damp environments. It is often eaten by fungivores.

ThingDef.label: churrun mast
ThingDef.description: A mast of pale fungus standing in the milk ponds, lit from inside with a cold blue-green light. It grows fast and cuts into mushroom logs, though not many; mostly it is the thing you steer by across the shallows.

ThingDef.label: churrun mast
ThingDef.description: Fast-growing, but doesn't yield much usable material. Aquatic fungus.

ThingDef.label: brommok timber
ThingDef.description: A massive marsh mushroom with a trunk as hard as wood, rooted in the milk ponds and growing fast enough to see. It cuts into ordinary wood, though not much of it for its size; it will only grow on soft, wet ground.

ThingDef.label: brommok timber
ThingDef.description: A strong wood-like mushroom. Fast-growing, but doesn't yield much usable material. It can only be grown by people on marshy soil.

ThingDef.label: tarrusk spire
ThingDef.description: A slow-growing mushroom tree with a purple-grey spire of a cap and a stalk as hard as good timber. It takes half a year to reach cutting size and is worth the wait: strong, straight, and handsome enough to build a hall from.

ThingDef.label: gubbra gourd
ThingDef.description: A gourd-like fungus, grey-green and bloated, that grows sacs of a foul-smelling liquid under its skin. Step on one and you will smell it for a day; nothing eats it, and nothing has to.

ThingDef.label: rustpuff
ThingDef.description: A large puffball mushroom that bursts at a touch into a cloud of flaky, rust-coloured spores. The spores stain everything and harm nothing; the forest floor is red-brown wherever a herd has walked through a patch.

ThingDef.label: tavvik crust
ThingDef.description: A tough, leafy crust-fungus that clings to rock and mat alike and survives on almost no light. Nothing much eats it and nothing much kills it; it is the last thing to go when the ground turns cold.

ThingDef.label: rhukk tooth
ThingDef.description: A large, blunt, tooth-white mushroom that beads and drips a red fluid thick as blood from every pore of its cap. It is harmless and it is not bleeding; nobody who sees one for the first time believes either.

ThingDef.label: rhessa cap
ThingDef.description: A broad crimson cap on a white stalk, the one saturated colour in a pale forest. It is good for nothing but looking at, and it is very good at that.

ThingDef.label: sylla lace
ThingDef.description: A grey fungus that grows a fine cloth-like lace from beneath its cap, hanging to the ground in a veil. The lace is cut and woven as cloth; it is the pale forest's only fabric, and it is better than it has any right to be.

ThingDef.label: dremmik cap
ThingDef.description: A large slow-growing mushroom that lives in symbiosis with a surprisingly tasty slime mold, which spreads in glimmering sheets across its cap and is scraped off and eaten. The mushroom takes a full season to mature; the slime comes back in days.

ThingDef.label: glimmerslime
ThingDef.description: Glimmerslime is a slime mold, not a real mushroom at all. It lives in symbiosis with the shinecaps.

ThingDef.label: tinnik bell
ThingDef.description: A small, pretty bell of a mushroom that glows a soft lantern-gold in the dark and gives a bite or two of edible fungus. Colonists plant them along paths for the light, and children pick them for no reason at all.

ThingDef.label: pursk hood
ThingDef.description: A big violet-capped mushroom whose cap folds down around the stalk like a hood. It is not very productive, but the hood is edible and it is everywhere, and that is enough.

ThingDef.label: vennik salve
ThingDef.description: A slow, delicate, honeycombed mushroom whose flesh is worked into fungal medicine. Sowing and harvesting it are both slow, careful work because the whole thing crumbles at a touch, and a crumbled one is worth nothing.

ThingDef.label: vennik salve
ThingDef.description: A slow-growing mushroom which yields fungal medicine when harvested. Sowing and harvesting this fungus are both very labor-intensive because of its delicate structure.

ThingDef.label: fungal medicine
ThingDef.description: A pack of fungal concoctions extracted from the mortal morel. It is less potent than industrial pharmaceuticals, but much better than nothing.

ThingDef.label: moonless stripes
ThingDef.description: Heat-loving and durable, this bizarre fungus thrives in the depths of the earth. While it can be grown anywhere, it requires high heat to grow properly and no light at all. Its sturdy layered stalk can be used as a leathery textile.

ThingDef.label: moonless leather
ThingDef.description: Tanned, dried, scraped mushroom layers. A good underground material for making clothes and bags.

ThingDef.label: tamma sweetcap
ThingDef.description: An oddly sweet mushroom grown in place of berries by everyone who lives under a roof of rock or spores. It tolerates cold, heat and filth, and its caps are eaten raw, dried, or stewed into the one dish every cantina on the night shoulder serves.

ThingDef.label: dulcis
ThingDef.description: Dulcis mushrooms. Nice to eat, even raw, if you like fungus.

ThingDef.label: kabbrik pod
ThingDef.description: A wild fungus whose swollen pods are packed with an oily spore-mass volatile enough to refine into chemfuel. It grows where it pleases and nowhere anyone plants it; it cannot be cultivated, or at least nobody has managed to.

ThingDef.label: blast spore sac
ThingDef.description: The spore sac of a blastpod fungus. It's a good fuel for campfires and generators, and can be refined into chemfuel.
